title: When Sales Rise and Margins Fall
summary: A fictional retailer sells more but keeps a smaller share of its sales as gross profit.

scenes.label: Revenue
scenes.headline: The retailer sells more
scenes.narration: Our fictional retailer grows quarterly sales from one hundred million dollars to one hundred and twenty million. That's twenty percent growth.

scenes.label: Cost of goods
scenes.headline: Inventory costs climb faster
scenes.detail: Illustrative quarterly cost of goods sold
scenes.narration: The cost of the goods it sold rises from sixty to seventy-eight million dollars. That's a thirty percent increase.

scenes.label: Gross margin
scenes.headline: Five cents less per sales dollar
scenes.detail: Illustrative gross profit divided by revenue
scenes.narration: Gross profit grows from forty to forty-two million dollars. But gross margin falls from forty to thirty-five percent because sales grow faster than gross profit.
